questions.q: The Rf of 2-methylpropene in ethyl acetate + ether is 0.42. It is treated with dilute H2SO4 to give the major product X. What is the Rf of X under identical conditions?
questions.explain: Dilute H2SO4 adds water across the double bond (acid-catalysed hydration). Protonation gives the most stable carbocation, the tertiary (CH3)3C+, which water attacks (Markovnikov). So X is tert-butyl alcohol, an alcohol with an OH group. OH can hydrogen bond with the silica plate, so the alcohol sticks to it more and moves less. Less movement means a lower Rf than the alkene's 0.42, so only 0.12 fits. The options 0.62 and 0.82 are traps: they would mean X is less polar than the alkene.

questions.q:
Statement I: Methane can be prepared by decarboxylation of sodium ethanoate, Kolbe's electrolysis of sodium acetate and reaction of CH3MgBr with water.
Statement II: Methane cannot be prepared from unsaturated hydrocarbons and by Wurtz reaction.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explain: Check each route for methane. Soda lime decarboxylation of CH3COONa gives CH4, and CH3MgBr + H2O gives CH4, so those two are fine. Kolbe's electrolysis of sodium acetate gives ETHANE (CH3-CH3) at the anode, not methane. That one wrong route makes Statement I false. Statement II is true: Wurtz joins two alkyl groups, so it needs at least two carbons to give ethane or higher, never methane. Unsaturated hydrocarbons also cannot give methane this way. So I is false and II is true.

questions.q:
Statement I: 3-phenylpropene on reaction with HBr gives a secondary alkyl bromide with a chiral carbon as the major product.
Statement II: Aryl chlorides and aryl cyanides can be prepared by Sandmeyer reaction as well as Gattermann reaction.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explain: 3-phenylpropene is Ph-CH2-CH=CH2. H+ adds to the terminal CH2 and gives the secondary cation Ph-CH2-CH(+)-CH3. A hydride shift then moves it next to the ring, giving the benzylic cation Ph-CH(+)-CH2-CH3, which is stabilised by resonance. Br- attacks there and gives Ph-CH(Br)-CH2CH3, a secondary bromide with a chiral carbon. So Statement I is true. Statement II is false as written: the Sandmeyer reaction uses CuCl or CuCN, and the Gattermann reaction uses Cu powder with HCl/HBr, so it makes aryl chlorides and bromides but not aryl cyanides. So I true, II false.

questions.q: An optically active alkyl bromide C4H9Br reacts with ethanolic KOH to form A. A on reaction with bromine gives B. B on reaction with ethanolic KOH and sodamide gives C. One molecule of water adds to C on warming with HgSO4 and dilute H2SO4 at 333 K to form D. Which test confirms the functional group of D?
questions.explain: Only one C4H9Br is chiral: 2-bromobutane. Ethanolic KOH eliminates HBr to give but-2-ene (A, the Saytzeff product). Br2 adds to give 2,3-dibromobutane (B). Double dehydrohalogenation with KOH and NaNH2 gives but-2-yne (C). Hydration with HgSO4/H2SO4 adds water, and the enol turns into the ketone butan-2-one (D). A ketone cannot give the silver mirror or Benedict test, which need an aldehyde. Lucas test is for alcohols. Butan-2-one has a CH3-CO- group, so it gives the iodoform (haloform) test.

questions.q: P is a C8H14 hydrocarbon. Ozonolysis of P gives Q. Q on refluxing with alkali gives R. R on treatment with I2/NaOH gives a yellow precipitate. Acidification gives S (shown). The correct structure of P is:
questions.explain: Work backwards from S, a cyclopentene acid with a CH3 and a COOH on the double bond. A yellow precipitate with I2/NaOH is iodoform, so R has a CH3CO- group. That group turns into COOH on S, which means R is 1-acetyl-2-methylcyclopentene. R forms from Q by an intramolecular aldol condensation under alkali, so Q must be a diketone. Q is CH3CO-(CH2)4-CO-CH3 (octane-2,7-dione), and its aldol closes a five-membered ring. Ozonolysis of a ring alkene gives exactly this chain, so P is 1,2-dimethylcyclohexene, which is C8H14. The other options give the wrong ring size or the wrong carbonyl pattern.

questions.q: Given are the alkenes: (A) 2-methylbut-2-ene, (B) cis-but-2-ene, (C) 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene, (D) prop-1-ene. Choose the correct stability order.
questions.explain: Alkene stability rises with the number of alkyl groups on the C=C. More alkyl groups mean more hyperconjugation (C-H bonds donating into the double bond) and more sp2-sp3 bonds. C is tetra-substituted, A is tri-substituted, and B (cis-but-2-ene) and D (prop-1-ene) are di- and mono-substituted respectively. So C > A comes first. B is di-substituted and D is mono-substituted, so B > D. Cis-but-2-ene has some steric strain, but not enough to fall below a mono-substituted alkene. Order: C > A > B > D.

questions.q: An alkene X on reductive ozonolysis gives HCHO (2 moles), OHC-CO-CHO and CH3-CO-CO-CO-CH3. Identify X.
questions.explain: Reductive ozonolysis cuts every C=C and puts a C=O on each end. Count the products: 2 HCHO (2 C), OHC-CO-CHO (3 C) and pentane-2,3,4-trione (5 C) make 10 carbons, so X is a six-membered ring with two =CH2 and two CH3 groups. The two exocyclic =CH2 groups give the 2 moles of HCHO and leave C=O on their ring carbons. Now cut the two ring C=C bonds. In D, one cut leaves a ring piece of CH, C=O, CH, which is OHC-CO-CHO. The other piece is CH3-C, C=O, C-CH3 with one more C=O, which is CH3-CO-CO-CO-CH3, three carbonyls in a row. Options A and B have only one ring C=C or the wrong spacing, and C splits into OHC-CO-CO-CH3 instead. Only D fits, which also matches the NTA key.
